customManagers.description: Tool versions in Dockerfile ARGs, marked with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above (cargo-chef, cargo-about). FanFicFare is in python/pyproject.toml + uv.lock (pep621 manager; lock file maintenance refreshes everything under it).
The BuildKit image CI builds with (image.yml, setup-buildx driver-opts), pinned by digest because its layer compression is part of the reproducible image digest.

packageRules.description: Base images: the Rust image and the Python image move independently of Cargo/pip, so keep them out of the dependency PRs.
GitHub Actions are pinned by commit; take them together.

A new runner OS can break the build in ways CI only half covers: propose it on the dependency dashboard and wait for approval. (The runtime base, distroless python3-debian13, only ever gets digest updates, which automerge; its next Debian release is a new image name, changed by hand.)

Automerge patch updates of stable (>= 1.0) dependencies once the required `ci-ok` check passes (GitHub auto-merge, enforced by the main ruleset). Minor and major updates, and patches of anything still on 0.x (where a patch may break), run CI and wait for a human. Digest and pin updates: next rule. Last on purpose, so no rule above overrides it. Lock file maintenance automerges too (top-level lockFileMaintenance). Each merge is a patch release (release.yml).

Digest and pin updates automerge too, at any version: the tag or version stays the same, only the digest it is pinned to changes (a rebuilt base image, a GitHub Action pinned to the commit of its tag).
